deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 49–51): Grothendieck studies objects (X, Σ, R). X is a compact oriented surface with boundary. Σ is a cut system, i.e. disjoint simple closed curves; Σ̃ is the cut-open circles. R is a finite set of marked points ('repères') on these circles. To each object he attaches a combinatorial 'graphe pendentif' Γ. Its vertices are the pieces of X∖Σ. Its edges A ≅ π0(Σ̃) are the cut circles, plus dangling ('libres') edges A_ℓ ≅ π0(∂X) for the boundary circles. A⃗ is the set of oriented edges, with orientation-reversal involution, and ω(a) is the fibre of A⃗ over a.

On p.49 the marking is encoded as follows. For each edge a there is R_a = R ∩ Σ̃_a. For each orientation ω ∈ ω(a) there is a cyclic permutation u_ω ∈ Circ(R_a), with u_{ω'} = u_ω^{-1} for the opposite orientation. Equivalently, R_a is a torsor under Z/r(a) twisted by the orientation sign.

This page continues that discussion.
(i) For a free edge (a boundary circle C ∈ π0(∂X)) the structure is already oriented: one of the two orientations in ω(a) is singled out, namely the boundary orientation.
(ii) For an ordinary edge, the data amount to a combinatorial polygon P_a. Its vertex set is R_a, and its edge set is canonically described from R_a, ω_a and ω_a → Circ(R_a).
(iii) Grothendieck then proposes a more convenient enriched encoding, which replaces the family (R_a) by a 'combinatorial contour'. This is a set R⃗ of 'repères de rigidification' with an action of the infinite dihedral group D∞ = ⟨σ0, σ1 | σ0² = σ1² = 1⟩. It comes with a map R⃗ → A⃗ that is equivariant along ε: D∞ → {±1}, where each σ_i acts on A⃗ by orientation reversal. For the free edges one adds a subset R⃗⁺_ℓ ⊂ R⃗|A⃗_ℓ fixing the orientation of the corresponding boundary contours.

In modern terms, R⃗ is the set of flags (point, adjacent arc) of the polygons P_a, equivalently (marked point, direction). σ0 moves to the other endpoint of the arc and σ1 to the other arc at the same point. Both reverse the induced orientation of the circle, which is exactly the ε-compatibility. Each D∞-orbit is the flag set of one polygon (a 2r-element orbit, with D∞ acting through the dihedral group D_r).

On p.51 this produces the groupoid of 'graphes pendentifs à repères' and a functor from the paradigm groupoid of surfaces with cuts and marks to it. The stated purpose is to make the gluing operation explicit and to find a purely algebraic-combinatorial description of the Teichmüller-type groupoids. Gluing here is the 'Lego' construction of the Teichmüller tower.
errors: Gap: an edge with R_a = ∅ (a cut circle carrying no marked point) gives an empty D∞-orbit. The flag encoding then loses the edge's polygon data, although the map to A⃗ need not be surjective. Grothendieck does not say whether every circle is required to carry a repère.

Degenerate cases r(a) = 1, 2 (flagged in the NB on p.49): for r = 1, σ0 = σ1 on the 2-element orbit. The encoding still works, but the 'polygon' P_a is degenerate (a loop or a digon). This is consistent but not discussed on the page.
The subset R⃗⁺_ℓ must be a section of the orientation choice, i.e. a union of ⟨σ0σ1⟩-orbits mapping onto one orientation. This is implicit, not stated.

ideas.what: Encoding marked points on cut/boundary circles by cyclic orders twisted by orientation, equivalently combinatorial polygons P_a attached to the edges of the dual graph of a cut system
ideas.modern_name: Marked (extended) surfaces with parametrized/marked boundary; edge data of the dual graph of a pants/cut decomposition
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §§2–3 in outline (Teichmüller tower, Lego game); not in this combinatorial detail

ideas.what: Replacing the R_a by a D∞-set R⃗ of flags with an ε-equivariant map to the oriented edges A⃗
ideas.modern_name: Flag/dart encoding of maps; the 1-dimensional cartographic group C_1 = D∞
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tutte, Jones–Singerman (1978); Grothendieck's cartographic groups C_n (Esquisse 1984); Malgoire–Voisin
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (cartographic groups C_2, and C_n in general)

ideas.what: Free/dangling edges for boundary components, with a distinguished orientation via R⃗⁺_ℓ
ideas.modern_name: Ribbon/fatgraphs with legs (half-edges) for boundary circles
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Penner, Kontsevich, modular operads of Getzler–Kapranov)

missed.claim: In the 1983 Teichmüller notes, before the Esquisse, Grothendieck already uses an infinite-dihedral-group set (the 1-dimensional cartographic group) to rigidify the marked points on cut circles. This links the cartographic/dessin formalism with the Lego-Teichmüller marking data. Later literature (Bakalov–Kirillov, Funar–Gelca) encodes marked points on cut circles by other means and does not phrase them via a D∞-set over the oriented dual graph.
missed.quote: un ensemble de repères R⃗ (dits "repères de rigidification"), sur un opérateur de D∞ = {σ0, σ1 | σ0² = σ1² = 1} dessus, et une application R⃗ → A⃗ compatible avec l'hom. D∞ → {±1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a uniform 'cartographic' combinatorial model of the objects of the Lego-Teichmüller groupoid. It also documents a historical precursor of the C_n formalism within the Teichmüller programme. It is of modest technical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a careful combinatorial bookkeeping device (flags with a D∞-action) that is essentially standard. The mildly notable point is its early appearance (1983) inside the Teichmüller-tower notes as the 1-dimensional cartographic group, used to rigidify cut-system markings, which appears undocumented.
transcription_corrections: 'arête Cibas' / 'arêtes Cibas' should almost certainly read 'arête libre' / 'arêtes libres' (dangling edges corresponding to π0(∂X)).
'spines R⃗ (dits "spines de rigidification")' should read 'repères R⃗ (dits "repères de rigidification")', consistent with 'graphe pendentif à repères' on p.51.
'on [?] choisit de l'une des deux orientations' is roughly 'on dispose de l'une des deux orientations' (the boundary orientation is given).
'sur un opérateur de D∞ dessus' should read 'avec un opérateur de D∞ dessus' (i.e. with a D∞-action).
'l'on dicte en somme' is likely 'l'on obtient en somme' or similar; 'polygonale combinatoire' is probably 'polygone combinatoire'.
'Il peut être plus commode de ... d'enrichir la structure': the leading 'K' is probably 'Il'.
Final line: 'définissant une orientation des contours correspondants'.
Top glyph 𝓕 is probably a page marker (e.g. '7' or 'F'), since the next page is headed '8'.
